name: Nodular Regenerative Hyperplasia of the Liver

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Histopathological Diagnostic Criteria for Nodular Regenerative Hyperplasia

criteria.description: Presence of multiple regenerative hepatic nodules without fibrosis on liver biopsy
No histological evidence of cirrhosis or significant fibrosis
Clinical or radiological evidence of portal hypertension (e.g., splenomegaly, varices)
Imaging showing multiple small hepatic nodules with preserved liver architecture

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of regenerative nodules without fibrosis plus absence of cirrhosis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily histological; imaging and clinical features support diagnosis

pathognomonic.symptomName: Hepatic regenerative nodules detected on biopsy
searchTerms: small liver growths found in biopsy
high blood pressure in liver veins
tiredness from high portal vein pressure
weakness due to increased portal pressure
platelet drop due to spleen trapping
blood loss due to swollen digestive veins

laboratory: Normal or mildly elevated liver enzymes
Normal synthetic liver function tests in early stages
imaging: Ultrasound or CT showing multiple small hepatic nodules without cirrhosis
Doppler ultrasound may show portal hypertension signs
MRI with nodular liver architecture without fibrosis
genetic: No specific genetic mutations identified; may be associated with autoimmune or vascular disorders
other: Liver biopsy demonstrating nodular regenerative hyperplasia without fibrosis is diagnostic

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of fibrosis and architectural distortion on biopsy
Elevated liver enzymes and impaired synthetic function
Obstruction of small hepatic veins on histology
Rapid onset of hepatomegaly and ascites
History of chemotherapy or bone marrow transplantation
Imaging evidence of portal vein obstruction
Absence of regenerative nodules on biopsy
Acute abdominal pain and rapid clinical deterioration

redFlags: Rapid onset of ascites or hepatic decompensation
references: Wanless IR. Nodular regenerative hyperplasia: a widespread lesion in portal hypertension. Hepatology. 1990.
Orphanet: Nodular Regenerative Hyperplasia of the Liver. ORPHA:48372.
Schouten JN, et al. Nodular regenerative hyperplasia: a rare cause of noncirrhotic portal hypertension. World J Hepatol. 2011.
